md_docs_2host-designation(3) Library Functions Manual md_docs_2host-designation(3)

NAME

md_docs_2host-designation - Discovery host designation

ACDS is authoritative about the current host. Host election and quality policy remain in the existing handoff implementation.

A joined connection may announce only its own participant ID in its own session. ACDS accepts the announcement only when its host ID and generation match the current handoff authority, including its committed round. Before a handoff exists, authority is initialized from the persisted host, or the session initiator. The endpoint must be terminated, have a nonzero port and a known connection type. An empty address uses the connection source address, as session creation already does. Once accepted, an endpoint is immutable within a committed decision; a conflicting replacement is rejected. An exact duplicate can repeat delivery.

Authority validation, database updates and fanout are serialized with handoff commits using the existing handoff mutex. HOST_DESIGNATED goes to every joined connection in the session, including the announcing host, through the existing pinned registry visitor. Other sessions and connections that have not joined are excluded. Individual failed sends are logged without stopping delivery to others. A subsequent announcement can repair delivery; a joining/reconnecting participant receives the persisted designation immediately after SESSION_JOINED.

Addresses follow the same disclosure rule as SESSION_JOINED: only password protected sessions or sessions with explicit public IP exposure disclose them. WebRTC participants can reconcile by participant ID without an address.

HOST_ANNOUNCEMENT and HOST_DESIGNATED include a 32-bit handoff generation in network byte order, initially one, plus the committed handoff round (initially zero). The pair orders decisions: multiple hosts may be committed within one membership generation. Preparing a successor does not advance the current host decision. The extended payload requires matching client/server versions; old announcement sizes fail closed. The generation is scoped to the active ACDS handoff lifetime, not a durable epoch across ACDS restarts.

Clients consume designations on the ACDS signaling transport, validate exact size, session, endpoint and generation, and ignore stale or duplicate authority. An endpoint-less designation may be completed by an endpoint for the same host and generation. Repeated handoff commits also cannot queue another teardown. An unchanged host updates metadata without restarting healthy media. A changed host uses the existing deferred role dispatcher, which joins media workers before releasing transports. TCP participants wait for a disclosed replacement endpoint; WebRTC participants can switch by host ID.

An actual host change uses the shared NOTICE_ANNOUNCE component with “The session has a new host.” It does not capture input, require acknowledgment, or introduce a modal popup over live video. Initial joins and duplicate events stay quiet. This is related to #280 (popup windows) and #297 (OS notifications). It does not implement a generic popup/help refactor or platform OS notifications.

Telemetry uses the existing OpenTelemetry adapter. Host-selection spans distinguish initial negotiation from successor decisions, with selected/committed/failed outcomes, generation/round, eligible candidate count and the selected candidate's upload/NAT quality. Selection, commit and failure counters and a recovery-duration histogram record decisions rather than periodic ticks. Recovery duration measures observed host loss to commit/failure, rather than media resumption. Designation/reconciliation spans describe announcement/replay/commit sources, accepted/ignored/failed outcomes and local role. Ignored designation and applied role-change counters distinguish duplicates from actual transitions. Broadcast-attempted means the registry visit completed, not that every recipient acknowledged delivery. Attributes omit session strings, participant identifiers and network addresses.
